headline: Southborough boards advanced the FY27 budget and warrant articles, backing an 8.8 million dollar Trottier Middle School roof replacement while deferring major road borrowing.
synopsis: Town boards completed critical preparations for the April 11 Annual Town Meeting, with the Advisory Committee recommending a 73.5 million dollar FY27 town budget after deferring 820,000 dollars for Atwood site remediation to the fall. The Select Board and the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee endorsed an 8.8 million dollar Trottier Middle School roof replacement, which will require a two-thirds Town Meeting vote and a May debt exclusion ballot question. Both committees withheld recommendations on a proposed 22 million dollar road and sidewalk bond pending detailed financial and debt impact presentations. Meanwhile, actuarial reports delivered to municipal and regional school officials revealed growing retiree health care liabilities, including a net liability of 54.4 million dollars for the town.

highlights.title: Trottier Middle School roof replacement project
highlights.why: Officials endorsed an 8.83 million dollar roof replacement eligible for 41.32 percent state reimbursement, requiring Town Meeting approval and a ballot debt exclusion.

highlights.title: FY27 operating and capital budget review and vote
highlights.why: The Advisory Committee recommended an overall budget of 73.46 million dollars for Town Meeting, voting to postpone an 820,000 dollar Atwood remediation project to the fall.

highlights.title: Road and sidewalk infrastructure bonding recommendation deferred
highlights.why: The Capital Committee withheld its recommendation on a 22 million to 25 million dollar road bond until Town Meeting to review debt service schedules and contracting plans.

highlights.title: Town retiree health care liabilities surge to 54.4 million dollars
highlights.why: Actuaries reported that Southborough's net OPEB liability jumped to 54.4 million dollars, driven by an 88 percent rate increase in municipal Medicare Advantage premiums.

highlights.title: Elementary School Building Committee structure established
highlights.why: The Select Board and School Committee established a five-member panel with three Select Board and two School Committee appointees to explore Neary School project options.

highlights.title: Route 9 District Improvement Financing district mapped
highlights.why: The committee modeled a proposed funding district covering 580 parcels along Route 9 to use commercial tax growth to pay debt service on future wastewater infrastructure.

looking_ahead.what: Planning Board public hearings on zoning warrant articles including the ADU bylaw
Advisory Committee meeting to review remaining articles and draft the voter letter
Joint Select Board and School Committee candidate interviews for the Elementary School Building Committee
Select Board debt presentation on road borrowing impacts
Continued hearings on 34 Turnpike Road and 250 Turnpike Road (Park Central 40B)
Annual Town Election ballot vote including Trottier roof debt exclusion
